core_obligations: By the declared input, E = Rf_*O_X is perfect, its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and it has tor amplitude in [0, infinity).
Base change gives H^0(E tensor kappa(s)) = H^0(X_s, O_{X_s}) = kappa(s) by hypothesis, so O_S -> E induces an isomorphism after tensoring with each kappa(s).

H^0(E) tensor kappa(s) -> H^0(E tensor kappa(s)) is surjective for every s; apply the cut-in-two lemma locally on S to split E = H^0(E) + tau_{>= 1}E with tau perfect of tor amplitude in [1, infinity).
Tor amplitude [0, infinity) makes H^0(E) flat; flat and perfect gives finite locally free.
O_S -> H^0(E) is an isomorphism: check after tensoring with residue fields by the flat-cokernel criterion, where it holds by the base-change computation.
proof_roadmap: Perfect pushforward setup; fibre computation; cut-in-two splitting; finite locally free; residue-field verification.
difficulty_reason: A splitting argument whose engine is the cut-in-two lemma plus residue-field bookkeeping; each step named.
